SMTO-MAN-0007 — The SMTO Manual changed while it was being read

GUID: 00a27ddc-93fc-5794-8fa9-724e05ddfe81
Slug: docs-stale-cursor
Domain: MAN · Subsystem: docs

What happened

  • SMTO was reading a long Manual page or list in parts, and the Manual was updated in between. The saved place no longer matches, so reading stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to open the Manual page or list again from the start. A fresh read uses the current Manual, so all its parts match each other.
  2. If it happens again soon after SMTO starts, wait a minute before asking. Shortly after starting, SMTO finishes preparing extra Manual reference pages in the background, which updates the Manual once.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the whole page or list without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to repeat the request over and over in quick succession; it won't help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Manual continuation cursor carries a corpus revision that differs from the current snapshot, for example after the generated reference pages were published.

What this means

  • A decoded continuation token carries a corpus revision different from the snapshot used for this request. Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.

Why this can happen

  • A decoded continuation token carries a corpus revision different from the snapshot used for this request.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the request's corpus revision with the token's issuing snapshot.

How to fix it

  • Restart the fetch or list call without a cursor so it binds to the current corpus revision, then follow its next_cursor values; never reuse a cursor across revisions.
  • Fetch or list again without a cursor using the current corpus revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Fetch or list again without a cursor using the current corpus revision.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh retrieval starts without the stale cursor and continues on one current revision.

What not to do

  • Do not invent references, read arbitrary files through Docs or retry in a tight loop.

Technical notes

  • Manual lookup diagnostics describe local snapshot availability and validation. They neither fetch external documentation nor rebuild content during rendering; generated-lane failure does not invalidate an available authored corpus.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
